note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in AZ.json, gathered 2026-10-04 (ADOT lists and corridor management plans, USFS, NPS, Yavapai County and Wikipedia).

byways.name: Historic Route 66 All-American Road (Topock to Ash Fork)
byways.where: Oatman Road, SR 66 and Mohave and Yavapai county highways from Topock on the Colorado River through Oatman, Kingman, Peach Springs and Seligman to Ash Fork

facts.fact: ADOT lists this segment as 152 miles on Mohave County Highway, Oatman Road, State Route 66 and Yavapai County Highway, with Oatman and Grand Canyon Caverns among its points of interest.
West of Kingman the old highway crosses the Black Mountains at Sitgreaves Pass, elevation 3,550 feet, then makes a slow winding descent.
Oatman began as a gold camp in 1915 and survives as a Route 66 stop with wooden sidewalks and wild burros wandering the streets.
SR 66 between Kingman and Seligman passes through Peach Springs, headquarters of the Hualapai Indian Reservation.

byways.name: Coronado Trail National Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 191 (with US 180) from Clifton north through Morenci, Hannagan Meadow and Alpine to Springerville and Eagar; Greenlee and Apache counties

facts.fact: The 103-mile section of US 191 between Clifton and Eagar is designated the Coronado Trail Scenic Road; the highway was signed US 666 until it was renumbered US 191 in 2003.
North of Clifton the route runs 14.22 miles through the Morenci mine on a temporary designation, and its serpentine alignment includes switchbacks in the mountains near Alpine.
ADOT lists the Morenci open pit copper mine, Hannagan Meadow and Nelson Reservoir among the road's points of interest.

byways.name: Desert to Tall Pines Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 288 (with Forest Road 512) from SR 188 near Roosevelt Lake north through Young; Gila County, Tonto National Forest

facts.fact: The Tonto National Forest describes 74 miles of SR 288 designated as a scenic byway through several biotic communities; not all sections are paved and some areas get heavy winter snow. Pleasant Valley Cemetery is a common stop.
Most of SR 288 is unpaved; the route was established in 1959 and received scenic road designation in 2001.
Young sits in Pleasant Valley and played a central part in the Pleasant Valley War between 1887 and 1897.

byways.name: Dry Creek Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 89A, about 6.5 miles running southwest from Sedona toward Cottonwood (MP 363.5 to 370.0)

facts.fact: ADOT's SR 89A corridor plan describes the Dry Creek Scenic Road as 6.5 miles running southwest out of Sedona; between mileposts 366 and 367 the highway crosses Dry Creek, the segment's namesake, and red rock vistas grow more dominant looking east toward Sedona.
The Dry Creek Scenic Road (US 89A, MP 363.5 to MP 370.0) was designated on January 15, 1993.
Before reaching Sedona, SR 89A provides access to Red Rock State Park.

byways.name: Jerome-Clarkdale-Cottonwood Historic Road
byways.where: Historic US 89A from the west end of Jerome through Clarkdale to the east side of Cottonwood, including Main Street in Cottonwood; Yavapai County

facts.fact: ADOT's corridor plan describes the historic road as 10 miles from the west end of Jerome through Clarkdale to the east side of Cottonwood; Jerome, an old mining town turned artist village, clings to Cleopatra Hill.
Jerome, built on Cleopatra Hill at more than 5,000 feet, was supported by rich copper mines; the mines closed for good in 1953 and the population fell below 100.
Tuzigoot is a roughly 1,000-year-old, 110-room hilltop pueblo built by the Sinagua in the Verde Valley.

byways.name: Joshua Forest Scenic Road (Wikieup to Wickenburg)
byways.where: US 93 from Wikieup (MP 126.5) south to about 20 miles north of Wickenburg (MP 180); Mohave and Yavapai counties

facts.fact: The 54 miles of US 93 between Wikieup and Wickenburg run through Joshua trees and the ecological boundary of the Mohave and Sonoran deserts, and were recognized as the Joshua Forest Scenic Road in 1993.
ADOT's draft corridor plan says the southern end of the corridor is a dense forest of Joshua trees, the largest of the yuccas.
North of the Santa Maria River the highway crosses Burro Creek on dual steel arch bridges about 400 feet above the intermittent stream.

byways.name: Mingus Mountain Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 89A from Yaeger Canyon on the Prescott Valley side over Mingus Mountain to the west end of Jerome (MP 332.0 to 343.5); Prescott National Forest, Yavapai County

facts.fact: ADOT's corridor plan describes 11.5 miles through the Prescott National Forest, starting in Yaeger Canyon at the base of the Black Hills, with ponderosa pine along the climb, many switchbacks, and views of the Mogollon Rim and Verde Valley from the summit.
The Mingus Lookout Complex, a fire tower and associated buildings at the top of Mingus Mountain, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Prescott National Forest's Mingus Mountain area, at 7,810 feet, is used for camping, hiking, hang gliding and paragliding, and has a small trout lake.

byways.name: Red Rock All-American Road
byways.where: SR 179 from I-17 (exit 298) north through the Village of Oak Creek to SR 89A in Sedona; Yavapai and Coconino counties

facts.fact: SR 179 runs 7.5 miles from I-17 to Sedona and received the All-American Road designation in 2006 for the red rock and sandstone formations it passes.
ADOT's corridor plan notes that Bell Rock adjoins the road, Cathedral Rock is reached via SR 179, and the Chapel of the Holy Cross is a dominant feature high in the red rock cliffs.
The Red Rock Scenic Road (SR 179) was designated a state scenic road on February 20, 1987.

byways.name: Swift Trail Parkway
byways.where: SR 366 from US 191 south of Safford up the Pinaleño Mountains toward Mount Graham; Graham County, Coronado National Forest

facts.fact: The Swift Trail, named for T. T. Swift, first supervisor of the Coronado National Forest, climbs from Sonoran desert at 2,900 feet to forests on the 9,000-foot ridges of the Pinaleño Range, and was built during the Great Depression by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
SR 366 is 28.33 miles long; it was a gravel road when established in 1960, and the easternmost 21.7 miles have since been paved.
ADOT's corridor plan gives Mount Graham's elevation as 10,713 feet and notes that forest roads beyond the state highway reach Riggs Flat Lake, an 11-acre lake in alpine forest.

byways.name: Walker Scenic Road
byways.where: Yavapai County Route 57 (Walker Road), milepost 0.35 to 7.82, to the settlement of Walker

facts.fact: ADOT lists Walker Scenic Road as 7.5 miles of County Route 57, with Lynx Creek Ruins, the site of Howell's smelter (1882) and the Bank Vault Mine among its points of interest.
Yavapai County adopted Walker Road as a county Scenic/Historic Route on June 21, 2023.
Walker, at about 6,289 feet, was named for the mountain man Joseph R. Walker; it had 200 people in 1890 and 39 in 1920.

byways.name: Diné Tah (Among the People) Scenic Road
byways.where: Navajo Route 12 from Lupton north through Window Rock, Fort Defiance and Tsaile, then Navajo Route 64 west to near Chinle; Navajo Nation, Apache County (briefly crossing into New Mexico near Navajo)

facts.fact: ADOT's corridor plan describes about 100 miles of Navajo Routes 12 and 64, beginning at Lupton and ending just outside Chinle near Canyon de Chelly National Monument; the route was renamed Diné Tah (Among the People) Scenic Road in May 2001, and Canyon del Muerto follows N64 between Chinle and Tsaile.
The same plan places Wheatfields Lake, at about 7,300 feet, along N12 about 44 miles northeast of Window Rock, among mountains, old cinder cones, pine forest and meadows.
Window Rock, capital of the Navajo Nation, is named for its sandstone window formation.

byways.name: Fredonia-Vermillion Cliffs Scenic Road
byways.where: US 89A from near Bitter Springs across Navajo Bridge and along the Vermilion Cliffs, over the Kaibab Plateau at Jacob Lake to Fredonia

facts.fact: ADOT's corridor plan says US 89A crosses the Colorado on Navajo Bridge, about 467 feet above the river, then runs along the base of the Vermilion Cliffs through House Rock Valley and climbs the Kaibab Plateau to more than 7,900 feet before descending to Fredonia at about 4,600 feet.

The 1928 Navajo Bridge, which replaced the Lees Ferry crossing, is now reserved for pedestrians beside the 1995 highway bridge; a road off the highway leads to the California condor release site, in use since 1996.
The Fredonia-Vermilion Cliffs Scenic Road (US 89A, MP 525.0 to 607.0) was designated on June 28, 1996.

byways.name: Historic Route 66 All-American Road (Ash Fork to Lupton)
byways.where: Former US 66 segments (Business I-40, US 89/180 and city and county roads) through Ash Fork, Williams, Flagstaff, Winona, Winslow, Joseph City and Holbrook toward Lupton at the New Mexico line; Coconino, Navajo and Apache counties

facts.fact: Old US 66 ran east into downtown Williams, where the Williams Historic Business District and Urban Route 66 are on the National Register of Historic Places, and southeast onto Second Street in downtown Winslow.
ADOT's designation list shows Historic Route 66 segments in Ash Fork, Williams, Flagstaff, Winona Road, Winslow, Joseph City and Holbrook, all designated on December 16, 1994.
Petrified Forest National Park protects one of the world's largest collections of petrified wood and a stretch of historic Route 66, along with the Painted Desert.

byways.name: Kaibab Plateau-North Rim National Scenic Byway
byways.where: SR 67 from Jacob Lake south across the Kaibab Plateau to the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park

facts.fact: SR 67 runs 31 miles from Jacob Lake to the North Rim; it was a Forest Service road and Territorial-period trail before joining the state system in 1941, was designated a state scenic road in 1985 and a National Scenic Byway in 1998.

The Forest Service describes high-elevation mixed conifer forest, sub-alpine meadows and ponds along the drive, with ponderosa pine, fir and quaking aspen; heavy snow normally closes SR 67 from November through mid-May.
The 44-mile drive from Jacob Lake to the North Rim is a designated National Forest Scenic Byway and State Scenic Parkway.

byways.name: Kayenta-Monument Valley Scenic Road
byways.where: US 163 from Kayenta north to the Utah line at Monument Valley (MP 389.0 to 416.7); Navajo Nation, Navajo County

facts.fact: ADOT's corridor plan notes that Agathla Peak (El Capitan), a remnant of volcanic activity, rises 1,500 feet above the desert floor beside the corridor, and that Monument Valley comes into view as you travel north toward the Utah border.
The same plan describes Goulding's museum as housed in the original 1920s trading post.
The Kayenta-Monument Valley Scenic Road (US 163, MP 389.0 to 416.71) was designated on June 28, 1996.

byways.name: Naat'tsis'aan-Navajo Mountain Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 98 from just south of Page southeast across the Navajo Nation through Kaibeto to US 160 near Shonto; Coconino County

facts.fact: ADOT's draft corridor plan says the byway, named Naat'tsis'aan 'Navajo Mountain' Scenic Byway in 2005, begins just south of Page and runs to US 160; a pullout at milepost 343 looks out to Navajo Mountain, a site sacred to the Navajo, Hopi and Paiute tribes.
Navajo Mountain's peak rises to about 10,388 feet.
Antelope Canyon is a slot canyon on Navajo land east of LeChee, near Page, and is the primary attraction of Lake Powell Navajo Tribal Park.

byways.name: San Francisco Peaks Scenic Road
byways.where: US 180 northwest from Flagstaff (MP 224.0 to 255.0) toward Valle; Coconino National Forest

facts.fact: ADOT lists the road as US 180, with Coconino National Forest, the Museum of Northern Arizona, Snowbowl and Lava River Cave among its points of interest.
US 180 passes through the San Francisco Peaks, the highest mountains in Arizona, on its way northwest from Flagstaff toward Valle.
The Forest Service describes the country around the peaks as pine forest, aspen groves and open prairie, with a forest road between Hart Prairie and Snowbowl meeting US 180.

byways.name: Sedona-Oak Creek Canyon Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 89A from Sedona north up Oak Creek Canyon to the rim at Oak Creek Vista (MP 375.5 to 390.0)

facts.fact: SR 89A through Oak Creek Canyon was the first state highway designated a scenic road by ADOT, on August 24, 1984.
The Forest Service describes a 15-mile canyon drive that climbs about 2,200 feet from Sedona, with switchbacks at the north end and stops at Midgley Bridge, Slide Rock State Park and Oak Creek Vista.
ADOT's corridor plan describes oaks, ponderosa pine and sycamores below towering red and white cliffs, and notes that Slide Rock State Park is one of the few homesteads in the canyon left intact.

byways.name: Tse'nikani-Flat Mesa Rock Scenic Road
byways.where: US 191 from south of Many Farms north through Round Rock and Rock Point to US 160 near Mexican Water (MP 467.0 to 510.4); Navajo Nation, Apache County

facts.fact: ADOT's draft corridor plan says the designated portion of US 191 runs from milepost 467.0, south of Many Farms, to milepost 510.4 at US 160 near Mexican Water, adjoining the Many Farms, Round Rock, Rock Point and Mexican Water chapters, and was named Tse'nikani 'Flat Mesa Rock' Scenic Road in 2005.
The Navajo Nation scenic byway listing describes red sandstone mesas, buttes and spires along this stretch of US 191.
ADOT lists the road as 45 miles of US 191.

byways.name: White Mountain Scenic Road
byways.where: A loop on SR 260, SR 261 and SR 273 near Eagar, Sunrise and Big Lake, with the SR 373 spur to Greer; Apache County, Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests and Fort Apache Indian Reservation

facts.fact: In 1993 Arizona designated parts of SR 260, SR 261 and SR 273 as the White Mountain Scenic Road, a 67-mile loop, plus the 4.6-mile Greer Highway (SR 373), through pine forests and open glades.
SR 273 passes Sunrise Lake and White Mountain Reservoir on its way to Big Lake and serves the Sunrise ski area.
Greer, founded around 1879 by Mormon settlers, sits at roughly 8,400 feet with the Little Colorado River running through town, the highest town in the state.

byways.name: White River Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 73 from Hon-Dah south to the Alchesay National Fish Hatchery (MP 346.85 to 357.72); Fort Apache Indian Reservation

facts.fact: In 1993 Arizona designated an 11-mile section of SR 73, from Hon-Dah south to the Alchesay National Fish Hatchery, as the White River Scenic Road; SR 73 between Fort Apache and Hon-Dah follows a territorial road, and an 1870s wagon road linked Fort Apache with its suppliers to the north and east.
Fort Apache Historic Park, a White Mountain Apache tribal park at the former fort about 4 miles south of Whiteriver, includes 27 historic buildings and the White Mountain Apache Cultural Center.
ADOT lists the Alchesay-Williams Creek National Fish Hatchery complex, the White Mountain Apache Cultural Center and Kinishba Ruin among the road's points of interest.

byways.name: Apache Trail Historic Road
byways.where: SR 88 from Apache Junction past Canyon Lake and Tortilla Flat through the Superstition Mountains to Theodore Roosevelt Dam and SR 188 (designated MP 201.0 to 242.5)

facts.fact: SR 88, one of Arizona's original 10 state highways (1927), began in 1904 as a wagon road to aid construction of Theodore Roosevelt Dam; most of the section between Fish Creek Bridge and Roosevelt Lake has never been paved.

Past Tortilla Flat the highway becomes an unpaved road winding east through the Superstition Mountains and follows the Salt River to Roosevelt Dam; after the 2019 Woodbury Fire and flood damage it was closed between mileposts 222 and 229 and reopened in September 2024.
Tortilla Flat is the last surviving stagecoach stop along the Apache Trail.

byways.name: Copper Corridor Scenic Road (SR 77)
byways.where: SR 77 (about 35 miles) in the San Pedro River valley north of Oracle through Dudleyville and Winkelman; designated as Copper Corridor Scenic Road East

facts.fact: ADOT lists this road as 35 miles of State Route 77, with Aravaipa Canyon Preserve, Biosphere 2 at Oracle and the Lower San Pedro River State Wildlife Area among its points of interest.
North of Mammoth, SR 77 crosses the San Pedro River and follows its east side through Dudleyville into Winkelman, where it crosses the Gila River next to the old Winkelman Bridge.
Copper Corridor Scenic Road East (SR 77) was designated on October 17, 2008.

byways.name: Copper Corridor Scenic Road (SR 177)
byways.where: SR 177 between Superior and Kearny, past the Ray mine and Kelvin (about 15 to 20 miles); designated as Copper Corridor Scenic Road West

facts.fact: A 15-mile segment of SR 177 was designated in 2008 as a scenic road for its geology; it passes the rough country south of Superior known as Apache Leap, the Dripping Spring Mountains and the open-pit Ray copper mine, with road cuts exposing copper-bearing strata.
Kearny was built by the Kennecott Mining Company in 1958 as a planned town for the people of Ray, Sonora and Barcelona, which were about to be swallowed by the expanding open-pit mine.
ADOT lists the road as 20 miles of State Route 177, with Kelvin Bridge and the White Canyon Wilderness among its points of interest.

byways.name: Gila-Pinal Scenic Road
byways.where: US 60 from near Florence Junction past Picketpost Mountain through Superior and the Queen Creek Tunnel to Miami (designated MP 214.5 to 240.5); Tonto National Forest

facts.fact: The Tonto National Forest describes 35 miles of US 60 past Picketpost Mountain, through Superior to Miami, crossing four biotic communities from Sonoran Desert to ponderosa pine, with Boyce Thompson Arboretum and riparian areas along Arnett and Pinto creeks.
The 1,217-foot Queen Creek Tunnel just east of Superior was completed in 1952, replacing the smaller 1926 Claypool Tunnel.
Superior was founded as a mining town for the Silver King and later Magma mines, first silver and then copper; the mountain above it is called Apache Leap.

byways.name: Organ Pipe Cactus Parkway
byways.where: SR 85 south of Why through Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument toward Lukeville (designated MP 57 to 78)

facts.fact: The Organ Pipe Cactus Parkway (SR 85, MP 57 to MP 78) was designated on December 19, 2008.
Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, an International Biosphere Reserve in the Sonoran Desert, is the only place in the United States where the organ pipe cactus grows naturally.
The monument was established in 1937, and SR 85 between Why and the border at Lukeville was paved in 1942 and 1943.

byways.name: Patagonia-Sonoita Scenic Road
byways.where: SR 82 from near Nogales northeast through Patagonia to Sonoita, then SR 83 north to I-10; Santa Cruz and Pima counties

facts.fact: SR 83 and part of SR 82 from north of Nogales to Sonoita form the Patagonia-Sonoita Scenic Road, the second road given scenic designation by Arizona; SR 83 served the Empire Ranch and the Kentucky Camp gold mine in the 1870s.

ADOT's corridor plan describes semidesert grassland and riparian woodland with cottonwoods along perennial streams, an abandoned railroad embankment along SR 82, and the Empire Ranch, which grew from a 160-acre homestead in the 1870s to almost a million acres by 1906.
The road (SR 82 MP 4.5 to 32.0 and SR 83 MP 33.0 to 58.0) was designated on September 20, 1985.

byways.name: Sky Island Parkway (Catalina Highway) National Scenic Byway
byways.where: Catalina Highway (General Hitchcock Highway, FS 833 with FS 10 and 11) from the northeast edge of Tucson up the Santa Catalina Mountains to Summerhaven and Mount Lemmon; Coronado National Forest

facts.fact: The Forest Service describes a 27-mile road climbing from the Lower Sonoran life zone to the forests of the Canadian zone; originally named the General Hitchcock Highway, it was begun in 1933 and completed in 1950, much of the labor supplied by a federal prison camp at the base of the mountain.

Along the drive are saguaro, mesquite and cholla at the bottom and fir and aspen on cooler north-facing slopes near the top; the road is the only paved route to Summerhaven, and the prison camp site became the Gordon Hirabayashi Recreation Area in 1999.
The Sky Island Parkway (FS 833, 10 and 11) was designated on August 17, 2001.
